statement_record.book: Definition 3.4.1, three clauses. For a diagram K : J -> C, F : C -> D (i) PRESERVES limits of K if the image of any limit cone over K is a limit cone over FK; (ii) REFLECTS limits of K if every cone over K whose image is a limit cone for FK was already a limit cone; (iii) CREATES limits of K if, whenever FK has a limit in D, K has a limit too, and a cone over K is a limit cone iff its image is. Extended to classes of diagrams and dualised to colimits.

statement_record.book: Definition 3.4.4: for a space X let O(X) be the poset of opens under inclusion. A family {U_i ⊆ U} COVERS U when the diagram of the U_i together with the inclusions of their pairwise intersections has colimit U in O(X). A presheaf F : O(X)^op -> Set is a SHEAF if it preserves these colimits, i.e. carries them to limits in Set; by Theorem 3.2.11 this is equivalent to F(U) -> prod_i F(U_i) => prod_{i,j} F(U_i ∩ U_j) being an equalizer diagram.
statement_record.intree: Sheaf X asks, for the single coverage family {fᵢ : uᵢ ~> u} chosen at each object u of an abstract Site C, that a compatible local section glue to a unique global section: '∃! x : X u, fmap[X] fᵢ x ≈ xᵢ'.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three independent ways. (1) No O(X): there is no poset-of-opens instance and no topological space anywhere in the tree, so the item's actual setting is not instantiated. (2) The 'covers' notion is a chosen coverage family with pullback stability, NOT 'the pairwise-intersection diagram has colimit U in O(X)' — covers are never characterised as colimits, and Site picks exactly ONE covering family per object (its own header calls this less general than a coverage). (3) The sheaf condition is stated as unique gluing, never as preservation of the covering colimit nor as the equalizer diagram; worse, Theory/Sheaf/Category.v lines 27-43 document that this predicate is PER-LEG and its compatibility antecedent forces xᵢ ≈ xⱼ for every section of the other leg, so it is satisfiable only when the fibres are subsingletons and vacuous at any covered object with two inequivalent sections.

gap: Missing: (a) O(X), the poset of open subsets of a topological space, as a category — no topological space is formalised in-tree at all; (b) the definition of 'covers' as 'the diagram of the U_i and their pairwise intersections has colimit U', i.e. covers-as-colimits; (c) the sheaf condition in Riehl's form, 'the presheaf carries these colimits to limits', and equivalently the equalizer diagram F(U) -> prod F(U_i) => prod F(U_i ∩ U_j) — the in-tree Sheaf is an unrelated unique-gluing encoding, itself documented (Theory/Sheaf/Category.v) as a per-leg approximation that is vacuous beyond subsingleton fibres.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the two defining clauses appear only as an instance, never as a definition. statement_record.book: Lemma 3.4.5: any full and faithful functor F : C -> D reflects any limits AND colimits that are present in its codomain. Proof: a cone lambda over K is a limit exactly when every cone mu factors uniquely through it; if F lambda is a limit cone then F mu factors uniquely through F lambda, and full faithfulness lifts the factorisation uniquely to C.
statement_record.intree: ff_reflects_limit: under Full F and Faithful F, given a cone N over G whose image apex carries a limit witness HL of F ◯ G with legs the image legs (Hlegs), the cone N itself is a limit of G — the mediator being the prefmap-preimage of the D-mediator, with both laws recovered from faithfulness.

statement_record.book: Lemma 3.4.6: any equivalence of categories F : C -> D preserves, reflects, and creates any limits and colimits present in its domain or codomain. Proof uses Lemma 3.4.5 for reflection and essential surjectivity plus full faithfulness for preservation and creation.
statement_record.intree: All six statements are proved for E : EquivalenceOfCategories F — equivalence_preserves_limits : PreservesAllLimits F and equivalence_preserves_colimits : PreservesAllColimits F (via RAPL/LAPC on the refined adjoint equivalence), equivalence_reflects_limits and equivalence_reflects_colimits (via ff_reflects_limit at Equivalence_Full/Equivalence_Faithful), equivalence_creates_limits : Limit (F ◯ G) → Limit G and equivalence_creates_colimits : Colimit (F ◯ G) → Colimit G (via the quasi-inverse's RAPL and limit_transport along quasi_inverse ◯ (F ◯ G) ≈ G).

statement_record.book: Proposition 3.4.8: for any object c of C the projection Pi : c/C -> C strictly creates limits and connected colimits; hence c/C has any limits and any connected colimits that C admits. The colimit half needs J connected, so that the lifted nadir mu_j . kappa_j is independent of j.
statement_record.intree: Comma_Complete: if C is complete and U : C ⟶ D preserves image limits, then the comma category =(d) ↓ U is complete, the limit being comma_limit whose apex is the C-limit paired with the unique mediator phi and whose legs project to the C-limit legs. Comma_Coslice identifies the coslice c ̸co C with =(c) ↓ Id in Cat.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three ways. (1) The result is stated for the general comma =(d) ↓ U and never instantiated at U := Id to give the coslice — no witness of PreservesImageLimit for the identity functor is produced, and Comma_Coslice is never used to transport completeness to c ̸co C. (2) The conclusion is COMPLETENESS of the comma category, not strict creation by the projection: nothing states that comma_proj2 lifts a given limit cone uniquely, nor that it preserves or reflects limits (the construction does exhibit the unique lift, but that fact is not a theorem). (3) The connected-colimit half is entirely absent: there is no colimit analogue of Comma_Complete and no notion of a connected category at all.

gap: Missing: (a) the instantiation at the coslice — Comma_Complete is never specialised to U := Id (no PreservesImageLimit Id witness) and never transported along Comma_Coslice, so 'c/C has the limits C has' is not stated for the coslice; (b) the strict-creation content — the theorem asserts only Complete (=(d) ↓ U), never that the projection creates (uniquely lifts) limit cones, nor that it preserves or reflects them; (c) the whole connected-colimit half of Proposition 3.4.8, which is doubly blocked, since neither a colimit analogue of Comma_Complete nor the definition of a connected category exists in-tree; (d) the Exercise 3.4.ii generalisation to categories of elements.
